instructions.question: What overall polarity does this French tweet convey about the situation, event or topic it reports (often ecology, energy, climate), reading its wording at face value?
instructions.rule: Positive needs an outcome framed as good: success, improvement, benefit, expansion of green capacity, approval, award, inauguration, protection, celebration, praise or advocacy (ironic praise counts literally), and also launches or public events (forum, summit, workshop, festival, talk) promoting a green, energy or sustainable theme. Negative needs harm, threat, decline, suspension, scandal, opposition, criticism or insult. A headline that merely presents a technology, sum, forecast or test is neutral, as are personal meetings, TV schedules, published figures, puns, banter and anecdotes.

neutral.what: Information without a framed outcome: descriptions of technologies, amounts, forecasts, tests, data, personal meetings, TV schedules, puns, chit-chat.
examples: Innovation : des tuiles transparentes pour capter l'énergie solaire http @user #energie (Innovation: transparent tiles to capture solar energy)
Un dispositif de stockage de l'#énergie solaire va être testé à #Lausanne #DD  http (A solar energy storage device will be tested in Lausanne)
En réunion avec Sébastien Cartier, Maire-Adjoint en charge de l'Écologie. (In a meeting with the deputy mayor for Ecology.)
"On peut vendre du vent, regarde les éoliennes" (You can sell wind, look at wind turbines)
neutral.cues: publie (publishes), réunion (meeting), sera l'invitée (will be the guest), va être testé (will be tested), pourrait (could), millions, ?, chiffres (figures), puns on vent (wind)
neutral.not_for: Success, benefit or expansion wording, or green-themed public events and launches, are positive; harm or suspension is negative.

positive.what: Achievements, improvements, benefits, expansions of green capacity, approvals, awards, inaugurations, launches and public events promoting green themes, protections, celebrations, praise, thanks, advocacy, or literal praise used ironically.
examples: Areva : Les 80 éoliennes du parc de Global Tech I installées avec succès http (Areva: the 80 turbines of the Global Tech I park successfully installed)
Des #eoliennes moins bruyantes grâce au hibou http #energie #innovation (Quieter wind turbines thanks to the owl)
Les Journées de l’Industrie électrique, c'est au Havre avec @user et dans 60 sites partout en France http #JIE2014 (The Electricity Industry Days are in Le Havre and at 60 sites across France)
Au Testet, la police stimule la croissance en coupant les arbres (At Testet, police stimulate growth by cutting trees)
positive.cues: avec succès (successfully), grâce à (thanks to), prometteuse (promising), accroître (increase), bientôt opérationnel (soon operational), inauguration, lancement (launch), sommet (summit), forum, journées (days), fête (festival), renforcées (reinforced), applaudissent (applaud), lauréat (winner), bravo, merci
positive.not_for: Bare presentations of a technology, sum or forecast, and personal meetings or TV schedules, are neutral.

negative.what: Threats, damage, deaths, decline, suspensions, scandals, opposition, criticism, anger or insults.
examples: Le manchot empereur victime du réchauffement climatique http (The emperor penguin, victim of global warming)
Suspension sine die de l'#ecotaxe http (Indefinite suspension of the ecotax)
@user Les éoliennes défigurent nos jolies campagnes. (Wind turbines disfigure our countryside.)
negative.cues: menacée (threatened), victime (victim), péril, suspension, scandale, enfer (hell), opposition, craintes (fears), détruit (destroyed), inutile (useless)
negative.not_for: Ironic praise phrased positively is positive; harmless jokes are neutral.
